solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: After tips were misplaced, pen did green line

indicators.note: the tips here are the end letters of each of the three words, which have gone missing

explanation.surface: Someone describes a writer who, losing pen nibs, drew a green line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips were misplaced' removes the last letter of each of pen, did and green, leaving PE, DI and GREE to run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedigree is a line of descent or ancestry, as in a family or breeding line.

clue.text: Imprisoned at the present time for five years

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means shut in or confined
AD, anno domini, marks the current era of dating

explanation.surface: A prisoner is serving five years at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (anno domini) labels the present era of the calendar, so it stands for 'at the present time'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentad is a group of five, including a span of five years.

clue.text: Regretted taking no time going the wrong way?

indicators.note: the built word goes the wrong direction, so it is read backwards
the word for regretted takes in other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it
O, a zero, means nothing or no

explanation.surface: Someone who regretted not allowing time ended up going the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts OT inside RUED to make RUOTED; 'going the wrong' way turns that round. The question mark flags the definition as a loose example.
explanation.definitionFit: A detour is a roundabout route, a way taken instead of the direct one.

clue.text: Good valley for taking exercise where fruit is grown

indicators.note: the valley word takes in the exercise letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a ravine is a narrow steep-sided valley
PE, physical education, is school exercise

explanation.surface: A fine valley for a workout happens to be where fruit grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercise' looks like part of the picture of a fit valley, but it supplies the school abbreviation; 'taking' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A grapevine is the plant on which grapes, a fruit, grow.

clue.text: Unconventional teen brat with new rifle?

definitions.text: Unconventional teen brat with new rifle?

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebellious teenager is pictured toting a brand-new gun.
explanation.walkthrough: TEENBRAT, N and RIFLE are rearranged together; the whole clue then describes such a youth.
explanation.definitionFit: An enfant terrible is a person whose unorthodox behaviour shocks others, the very picture of the clue.

clue.text: Not this on top of church?

definitions.text: Not this on top of church?

indicators.note: in a down-reading sense the first piece sits above the second, so it comes first

parts.note: the opposite of this is that

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether something other than this is up on the church roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on top of' means the first piece is placed before the second in the answer; the whole clue also pictures straw roofing above a country church.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is straw or reed roofing laid on top of a building, such as a rural church.

clue.text: Singing men's songs

indicators.note: when sung out, the sound of a word is what counts, not its spelling

parts.note: a jokey possessive of him, 'hims', meaning belonging to men

explanation.surface: A choir sings songs written for male voices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men's' read as 'him's', belonging to him, says HIMS, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hymns are religious songs of praise.

clue.text: Reluctantly abandon rebel

definitions.meaning: to tear yourself away is to leave unwillingly

explanation.definitionFit: Tear away is a phrasal verb for leaving reluctantly, while a tearaway is a reckless youngster.

clue.text: Well-built thug seen on TV

parts.note: a heavy is a hired tough or thug
a TV set, a television

explanation.surface: A muscular hoodlum appears on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavyset means stocky and solidly built.

clue.text: Rugby moves lifting equipment

definitions.meaning: blocking and tackling are defensive actions on the rugby field
a pulley system with ropes for hoisting loads

explanation.definitionFit: Block and tackle is a pulley-and-rope hoist; read literally it names two rugby actions.

clue.text: Greatly missing 50%

definitions.meaning: British slang for very much indeed, as in 'did you enjoy it? - ...!'

explanation.definitionFit: Not half is British slang meaning extremely or very much; read literally it means lacking a half.

clue.text: Surrounding a character in Greek dance

indicators.note: the Greek letter goes around the single letter, holding it inside

parts.note: lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek letter is sketched around a dancer's figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast Brazilian partner dance.

clue.text: Blue Arizona river

parts.note: AZ is the postal abbreviation for Arizona
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: An Arizona river is described as blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is a bright sky-blue colour.

clue.text: Fundamental as scenery in play

indicators.note: in play means put into motion, so these letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Stage scenery is described as essential to a theatrical production.
explanation.definitionFit: Necessary means essential or indispensable, so fundamental to something.

clue.text: Water droplets dripped on black stone put the wrong way

parts.note: mist is fine water droplets in the air
liquid that dripped ran
slate is a dark grey-black stone

explanation.surface: Water drips onto a dark stone slab placed badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistranslate is to render words wrongly into another language, putting them the wrong way.

clue.text: Mass for one man's crate is uncertain

indicators.note: uncertain means unsettled, so these letters are not in a fixed order

explanation.surface: A man is unsure about his crate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is uncertain' rearranges MANSCRATE; 'for one' marks Mass as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mass is one of the Christian sacraments, an example of the class.

clue.text: Mopping up looted goods holding black receptacle

indicators.note: the loot word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: swag is slang for stolen goods
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a bin is a container

explanation.surface: Stolen goods are being cleaned up along with a dark container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looted goods' is slang for stolen loot here; 'holding' is the container signal around the colour letter and the container word.
explanation.definitionFit: Swabbing means cleaning with a mop or swab, as on a ship's deck.

clue.text: Fortune teller has succeeded as songwriter

indicators.note: the fortune teller has the other letter inside, holding it

parts.note: a palmist reads fortunes from the lines of the hand
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A palm reader has found success as a writer of songs.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalmist is a writer of psalms, which are sacred songs.

clue.text: Sweat, perhaps?

parts.note: perspiration is something the body expels; also the letters of sweat come from shuffling a word meaning rubbish

explanation.definitionFit: Sweat is an example of a substance the body discards as unwanted output.

clue.text: Supporter is mean to suppress suffering

indicators.note: to suppress is to keep down or hold in, so the average word holds the other inside

parts.note: par is the average or mean standard
ill means unwell or suffering

explanation.surface: A backer is said to be unkind in keeping down someone's distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like unkind, but it is the average, as in par for the course; 'to suppress' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar is a column that holds up a structure, so a support.

clue.text: Insults crooked saint

parts.note: wound, past tense of wind, means twisted or crooked

explanation.surface: A dishonest holy figure trades insults.
explanation.definitionFit: To wound someone with words is to hurt or offend, as an insult does.

clue.text: Nearly ban alkali for dissolving a musical instrument

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something dissolving breaks up, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemist almost bans alkali for dissolving an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' leaves BA; 'dissolving' rearranges ALKALIA to LALAIKA.
explanation.definitionFit: The balalaika is a Russian stringed instrument with a triangular body.

clue.text: Ancient knowledge shrouds island valley

indicators.note: to shroud is to cover or wrap, so the knowledge word wraps the other letter

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge passed down

explanation.surface: Old legends surround an isolated valley.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire Valley in France is famed for its chateaux; the name refers to the river and its valley.

clue.text: A child loses foot to acid

indicators.note: foot means the end of the word, which is dropped

parts.note: a minor is a child in law

explanation.surface: A youngster loses a foot to a corrosive acid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses foot' cuts the last letter from MINOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Amino is short for amino acid, the building block of proteins.

clue.text: Firstly, in names, it transpires it's a letter

definitions.text: Firstly, in names, it transpires it's a letter

indicators.note: firstly tells the solver to take the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: It turns out that, at the start of names, one finds a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of the seven words after 'Firstly' spell the answer, and the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: An initial is the first letter of a name, which is just what the clue describes.

clue.text: Mistake using king to replace good castle

indicators.note: one letter is put in place of another in the word

parts.note: a gremlin is a fault or glitch that causes things to go wrong
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A blunder lets a king take over a fine castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' swaps the G of GREMLIN for K.
explanation.definitionFit: A kremlin is a Russian citadel or fortress, such as Moscow's.

clue.text: Extremely disappointed how fish is prepared

definitions.meaning: fish is cleaned by removing its innards

explanation.definitionFit: Gutted is British slang for bitterly let down, and also the state of a cleaned fish.

clue.text: They are worn by dancers in Cats with time for piano

indicators.note: time goes in for, meaning in place of, the piano letter in the word

parts.note: leopards are big cats
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: Dancers in the musical Cats swap rehearsal time for piano practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with time for' puts T in place of the P of LEOPARDS. 'Cats' looks like the musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Leotards are close-fitting one-piece garments worn by dancers and gymnasts.
